scoring_criteria.degree: Inadequate System - (SOP is not defined/ Not documented)
Partially Implemented (SOP defined, documented & implemented partially)
Implemented & Sustained (SOP defined, documented, strictly implemented & verified)

maturity_levels.criteria: Initial Phase – Minimal Awareness on Safety
Standard Phase - Documented and Systemic Safety Management
Proactive Phase- Risk Integrated & Continual Improvement
Resilient Phase- World Class Safety Culture & Excellence

cover_page.title: Comprehensive Safety Audit (CSA) Report - BPL Unit-1 (Bonthapalli)
cover_page.subtitle: Safety Management System & Process Safety Management Gap Assessment
cover_page.hazard_classification: Major Hazard Installation (MHI) - Class A Chemical

questions.checklist_observation:
Does the organization have EHS & Wellness policy? 
Whether the EHS & Sustainability policy reviewed periodically?
questions.auditor_verification:
Document Verification: 
Approved EHS & Wellness policy, version control, communication record.Review frequency defined, last review MOM, revision history.
Shopfloor Verification: 
Policy displayed at entry & work areas; employees aware of policy.Check whether updated policy displayed in departments.
questions.observation: EHS Policy is available and meets statutory requirements. Periodic review procedure exists but review frequency (timeline) is not mentioned in the document. Policy implementation framework is in place.
questions.recommendations: Mention specific review frequency  in EHS Policy document as per ISO 14001:2015 Clause 5.2.

questions.checklist_observation: Is EHS & Sustainability policy being displayed at prominent locations in the Unit in vernacular language? Whether the policy and safety systems is made to know to all?
questions.auditor_verification:
Document Verification: 
Policy communication record (induction, email).
Shopfloor Verification: 
Policy display boards across plant.
questions.observation: EHS Policy is displayed at entrance and prominent locations. All employees are trained on EHS Policy during induction. Policy is available in vernacular language.

questions.checklist_observation: Has a company-level EHS leader been designated?
questions.auditor_verification:
Document Verification: 
Appointment letter, roles & responsibilities.
Shopfloor Verification: 
Employees able to identify EHS leader; involvement visible in meetings.
questions.observation: Corporate EHS Head is designated with defined roles and responsibilities. Appointment letter is available.

questions.checklist_observation: Is EHS leadership is visible, active, and consistent in its support for EHS programs and objectives?  This leadership philosophy extends down through the ranks of middle management within the organization.
questions.auditor_verification:
Document Verification: 
Gemba walk logs, leadership participation records.
Shopfloor Verification: 
Observe leadership involvement in shopfloor activities.
questions.observation: Senior Leadership is involved in Safety Committee meetings and promotional activities. However, middle management engagement in EHS activities is limited.
questions.recommendations: Include EHS KPIs in middle management Job Descriptions. Conduct monthly EHS engagement sessions with supervisors as per ISO 45001:2018 Clause 5.1.

questions.checklist_observation: Does site senior management understand the technical aspects of EHS and Process Safety and how the EHS Standard is interpreted for the site/company?
questions.auditor_verification:
Document Verification:  
Leadership training records on PSM/EHS topics.
Shopfloor Verification: 
Interview leaders to assess understanding of risk controls.
questions.observation: Senior Management is aware of EHS and PSM requirements. However, implementation at shopfloor level is weak.
questions.recommendations: Conduct PSM awareness training for Senior Management. Implement top-down safety leadership program with quarterly reviews as per OSHA PSM 29 CFR 1910.119.

questions.checklist_observation: Are the core EHS values written down and stressed in training and other forums?
questions.auditor_verification:
Document Verification: 
EHS values documented in induction, TBTs, posters.
Shopfloor Verification: 
Check display boards, training rooms, communication kiosks.
questions.observation: EHS core values are communicated during Induction, TBTs, and other meetings. Values are documented and displayed.

questions.checklist_observation: Does the Leadership team exhibit their commitment towards EHS & Sustainability policy?
questions.auditor_verification:
Document Verification: 
Leadership review minutes, EHS discussions.
Shopfloor Verification: 
Interactions with employees reflect leadership focus.
questions.observation: Leadership commitment is visible through Safety Committee meetings, promotional activities, SOI Gemba walks, and R&R programs.

questions.checklist_observation:
Does Leadership team visibly demonstrate, by personal example, belief and commitment to EHS issues? 

EHS commitment is considered as –
• Communicating EHS expectations with employees, 
• Discussing and reviewing progress against EHS targets and 
• Participation in EHS activities.
questions.auditor_verification:
Document Verification: 
Safety meeting MOMs, communication mails.
Shopfloor Verification: 
Evidence of leadership presence during audits/meetings.
questions.observation: Leadership demonstrates commitment through Safety Committee meetings, Gemba walks, SOI observations, and R&R programs. SLT involvement is documented.

questions.checklist_observation: Does the site leadership team conduct safety Gemba walks on a monthly basis.
questions.auditor_verification:
Document Verification: 
Gemba walk schedule & reports.
Shopfloor Verification: 
Gemba observations closed in field.
questions.observation: Gemba walk schedule and records are available. Compliance with scheduled rounds is maintained.
questions.recommendations: Ensure 100% compliance with Gemba walk schedule. Track and close observations within 15 days.

questions.checklist_observation: Are EHS Lessons learned documents prepared? Is the same shared and promoted by leaders at all levels?
questions.auditor_verification:
Document Verification: 
Lesson learned documents shared.
Shopfloor Verification: 
Posters/alerts displayed in departments.
questions.observation: EHS lessons learned documents are not consistently prepared and shared across the organization.
questions.recommendations: Prepare EHS Lessons Learned documents for all incidents. Share via email, display on notice boards, and publish on company intranet.

questions.checklist_observation: Employees/staff commit a meaningful amount of time personally involved in safety activities (e.g. risk mitigation planning, discussing incident investigations, and actively monitoring action item tracking).
questions.auditor_verification:
Document Verification: 
Attendance in audits, meetings, campaigns.
Shopfloor Verification: 
On-ground participation during walkthroughs.
questions.observation: Employees are trained on safety equipment usage. Job descriptions include safety responsibilities. USCA and Near Miss reporting systems are in place.

questions.checklist_observation: Do the employees/staff review industry and company incidents and review their own operations for similar hazards? Are Safety topics regular agenda items at board/executive meetings?
questions.auditor_verification:
Document Verification: 
Incident learning review MOMs.
Shopfloor Verification: 
Check if key learnings are displayed.
questions.observation: Safety topics are regular agenda in board/executive meetings. However, review of industry incidents for similar hazards in own operations is not done systematically.
questions.recommendations: Establish monthly review of industry incidents. Share learnings in Safety Committee meetings and display key alerts at shopfloor.

questions.checklist_observation: Is the setting of EHS targets a proactive process (against a reactive process, with e.g.) and is the same carried out in consultation with staff and contract employees?
questions.auditor_verification:
Document Verification: 
Annual EHS target setting document, involvement evidence.
Shopfloor Verification: 
Check awareness of targets among employees/contractors.
questions.observation: EHS target setting process is in place. However, contract employees are not consulted during target setting as required under ISO 45001:2018 Clause 5.4.
questions.recommendations: Include contract employees in EHS target setting discussions. Conduct quarterly meetings with contractor supervisors as per ISO 45001:2018 Clause 5.4.

questions.checklist_observation: Is Safety leading and lagging metrics are tracked at the site and company level?
questions.auditor_verification:
Document Verification: 
KPI matrix, dashboards, MOMs showing review.
Shopfloor Verification: 
KPIs displayed in shopfloor boards/digital screens.
questions.observation: Safety leading and lagging metrics are tracked at site and company level. KPI dashboards are maintained.

questions.checklist_observation: Safety activities are included in annual operating plans and budgets.
questions.auditor_verification:
Document Verification: 
Budget allocation for EHS activities, financial approvals.
Shopfloor Verification: 
Evidence of funded safety upgrades implemented.
questions.observation: Safety activities are included in annual plans. Events like National Safety Day, Electrical Safety Day, and Fire Week are celebrated. However, shopfloor employees are not involved in RA and PHA exercises.
questions.recommendations: Involve shopfloor employees in Risk Assessment and PHA exercises as per ISO 45001:2018 Clause 5.4 and OSHA PSM 29 CFR 1910.119(e).

questions.checklist_observation: Safety metrics directly impact executive compensation.
questions.auditor_verification:
Document Verification: 
HR compensation policy, KPI linkages.
Shopfloor Verification: 
Leaders aware of safety-linked incentives.
questions.observation: Safety-based Job Descriptions are not available for employees and managers.
questions.recommendations: Develop and implement Safety-based Job Descriptions for all levels. Include EHS KPIs in performance appraisal as per ISO 45001:2018 Clause 5.3.

questions.checklist_observation: Employees/staff and Leadership team respond to poor safety performance with the intent to identify and address root causes.
questions.auditor_verification:
Document Verification: 
RCA reports, CAPA tracker.
Shopfloor Verification: 
Verification of CAPA closure in field.
questions.observation: R&R program exists for addressing poor safety performance. Root cause analysis is conducted for incidents.

questions.checklist_observation: Employees/staff and Leadership team reward good safety performance and identify learning to leverage across the site/company.
questions.auditor_verification:
Document Verification: 
Reward & recognition records.
Shopfloor Verification: 
Winners’ details displayed, events conducted.
questions.observation: R&R program is in place for recognizing good safety performance. Learning from good practices is shared.

questions.checklist_observation: The annual report discusses safety activities and leading safety metrics.
questions.auditor_verification:
Document Verification: 
Annual report EHS section.
Shopfloor Verification: 
Employees aware of achievements.
questions.observation: EHS activities and metrics are not included in the Annual Report.
questions.recommendations: Include EHS Policy, safety activities, and leading metrics in Annual Report as per GRI Standards and ESG reporting requirements.

questions.checklist_observation: Executive leadership routinely visits the facility and have meaningful discussions regarding safety related issues with operations and maintenance personnel.
questions.auditor_verification:
Document Verification: 
Visit logs, MOMs.
Shopfloor Verification: 
Cross-check with employees whether visits happen.
questions.observation: LDM and AET meetings are conducted. Leadership visits facility regularly.
questions.recommendations: Improve effectiveness of leadership visits. Document specific observations and track closure of action items.

questions.checklist_observation: Employees/staff personally follow-up with site operations and technical personnel regarding potentially significant safety incidents.
questions.auditor_verification:
Document Verification: 
Follow-up meeting MOMs.
Shopfloor Verification: 
Field verification of high-risk corrections.
questions.observation: Follow-up on safety issues is weak. Damaged insulations and corroded lines observed during audit indicating gaps in reporting and follow-up.
questions.recommendations: Improve awareness for reporting unsafe conditions. Establish weekly follow-up mechanism for pending safety observations.

questions.checklist_observation: Does the factory has a safety committee(s)? What are the types, structures and terms of reference of the committees?
questions.auditor_verification:
Document Verification: 
Safety committee constitution, statutory compliance.
Shopfloor Verification: 
Committee minutes displayed on boards.
questions.observation: Safety Committee meetings, Review meetings, and Townhalls are conducted with employees and contractors. However, Process Safety related issues are not discussed.
questions.recommendations: Include Process Safety topics (HAZOP findings, PSI updates, MOC status) in Safety Committee agenda as per OSHA PSM 29 CFR 1910.119.

questions.checklist_observation: Is the constitution of the safety committee(s) as per the statute?
questions.auditor_verification:
Document Verification: 
Notification, member list, legal compliance record.
Shopfloor Verification: 
Committee list displayed in admin/notice boards.
questions.observation: Safety Committee is constituted as per Factories Act 1948 Section 41-G and State Factory Rules.

questions.checklist_observation: How are the members of safety committee(s) selected? (elected / nominated)
questions.auditor_verification:
Document Verification: 
Election records / nomination approval.
Shopfloor Verification: 
Cross-check member names displayed on notice boards.
questions.observation: Safety Committee members are selected as per statutory requirements (elected/nominated).

questions.checklist_observation: How often are the meetings of safety committee(s) held?
questions.auditor_verification:
Document Verification: 
Meeting schedule + attendance.
Shopfloor Verification: 
Notice board shows meeting frequency.
questions.observation: Safety Committee meetings are held quarterly as per statutory requirement.

questions.checklist_observation: How are the recommendations of the committee implemented? Give details number of recommendation and implemented (minimum 50% completed).
questions.auditor_verification:
Document Verification: 
Action closure tracker.
Shopfloor Verification: 
Field closure of committee action items.
questions.observation: MOM is prepared and circulated to departments for compliance. However, some observations are pending closure for more than 5 months.
questions.recommendations: Establish 30-day closure timeline for Safety Committee recommendations. Escalate pending items beyond 30 days to Plant Head.

questions.checklist_observation: Do the employees/staff and leadership positively recognize individuals for raising concerns regarding safety.
questions.auditor_verification:
Document Verification: 
Suggestion scheme / reward records.
Shopfloor Verification: 
Recognition boards updated.
questions.observation: Suggestion boxes and USCA Near Miss reporting system are available. Employees are recognized for raising safety concerns.

questions.checklist_observation: Does the site EHS review meetings are being conducted by the site leadership team on a montly basis.
questions.auditor_verification:
Document Verification: 
Review agenda, KPI status updates, MOMs.
Shopfloor Verification: 
Action items visible on boards.
questions.observation: Site MRM meetings and Townhall meetings are conducted regularly by leadership team.

questions.checklist_observation: Are the recommendations of the site EHS review meetings implemented?
questions.auditor_verification:
Document Verification: 
CAPA tracker, MOM follow-up.
Shopfloor Verification: 
Check closed actions physically completed.
questions.observation: MOM is prepared and circulated to respective departments for compliance. Action tracking is in place.

questions.checklist_observation: Does a written program exist regarding employee participation?
questions.auditor_verification:
Document Verification: 
Check approved Employee Engagement program/SOP, version & scope.
Shopfloor Verification: 
Interview employees to confirm awareness of engagement activities.
questions.observation: No employee engagement program is in place.
questions.recommendations: Develop and implement an employee engagement program covering safety participation activities as per ISO 45001:2018 Clause 5.4.

questions.checklist_observation: Has roles been identified for each employee with respect to Safety?
questions.auditor_verification:
Document Verification: 
Verify R&R matrix, departmental responsibilities, job descriptions.
Shopfloor Verification: 
Ask employees if they know their safety roles (TBT participation, reporting).
questions.observation: Job descriptions and roles & responsibilities for safety are not documented.
questions.recommendations: Develop job descriptions with clearly defined safety roles and responsibilities for all employees as per ISO 45001:2018 Clause 5.3.

questions.checklist_observation: Does the line owners ensure and take responsibility for the effective implementation of EHS procedures across the site?
questions.auditor_verification:
Document Verification: 
Department-wise compliance reports, procedure implementation checklists.

Shopfloor Verification: 
Verify line owners performing checks in their areas.
questions.observation: No records available for line owners ensuring EHS procedures.
questions.recommendations: Conduct surprise inspections to verify line owners are ensuring PPE compliance and EHS procedure implementation. Maintain records as per Factories Act 1948 Section 7A.

questions.checklist_observation: Does the employee have knowledge on their repsective area/department  risk assessment?
questions.auditor_verification:
Document Verification: 
RA/JSA training records.

Shopfloor Verification: 
Ask employees to identify hazards in their work area.
questions.observation: Training has been provided.
questions.recommendations: Provide comprehensive, activity-based training covering all tasks, risks, and safety procedures in the specific area, including practical sessions.

questions.checklist_observation: Does cross functional teams have been consulted on the conduct and development of risk assessment?
questions.auditor_verification:
Document Verification: 
RA participation sheets, cross-functional attendance.

Shopfloor Verification: 
Ask area in-charge about involvement from QC/Engg/EHS.
questions.observation: Procedure is available.
questions.recommendations: Ensure CFT participation in RA to capture all operational, safety, and process risks.

questions.checklist_observation: Are control measures minimizing risk as identified in the Job Safety Assessment effectively communicated to all employees onsite, and documented?
questions.auditor_verification:
Document Verification: 
JSA communication sheets, acknowledgement records.

Shopfloor Verification: 
Verify actual control measures implemented in workplace.
questions.observation: Job Safety Analysis (JSA) is not available.
questions.recommendations: Develop and implement JSA for all hazardous activities. Provide training on JSA to employees as per OSHA 29 CFR 1910.119 and IS 14489:2018.

questions.checklist_observation: Are Tool Box Talks addressing the hazards of the work being performed carried out for the personnel?
questions.auditor_verification:
Document Verification: 
TBT schedule, attendance logs.

Shopfloor Verification: 
Confirm TBT board updated; observe ongoing TBT if possible.
questions.observation: Tool Box Talks (TBTs) are conducted.
questions.recommendations: Ensure hazards are effectively incorporated into TBTs. Conduct TBTs for every shift as per ISO 45001:2018 Clause 7.4.

questions.checklist_observation:
Has a system been evolved for the reporting of near misses and proposing of EHS relevant suggestions?
Has a reward scheme been initiated for the same?
questions.auditor_verification:
Document Verification: 
Near Miss log, suggestions register, closure record.

Shopfloor Verification: 
Check near miss display boards & availability of forms.
questions.observation: Suggestion boxes and USCA near-miss reporting system are in place.
questions.recommendations: Improve awareness of near-miss reporting among all employees through training and display boards as per Factories Act 1948 Section 41B.

questions.checklist_observation: Does EHS R&R Program is being implemeted across the site on a monthly basis.
questions.auditor_verification:
Document Verification: 
R&R criteria, monthly award records.

Shopfloor Verification: 
Posters of winners, employees aware of recognition scheme.
questions.observation: R&R program is available

questions.checklist_observation: Does the Progressive disciplinary measures for any violations / non-compliances are being implemeted across the site.
questions.auditor_verification:
Document Verification: 
Disciplinary procedure, records of actions taken.

Shopfloor Verification: 
Check if employees are aware of consequences; verify repeat violations closed.
questions.observation: RR&PDM procedure is available

questions.checklist_observation: Are employees encouraged and empowered to stop work in case of unsafe conditions or practices (“Stop Work Authority” policy)?
questions.auditor_verification:
Document Verification: 
Review Stop Work Authority policy & communication records.

Shopfloor Verification: 
Ask employees if they know they can stop unsafe work & if they've used SWA.
questions.observation: Stop Work Authority policy is not available.
questions.recommendations: Develop and implement Stop Work Authority policy. Train all employees on their right to stop unsafe work as per OSHA guidelines and ISO 45001:2018 Clause 5.4.

questions.checklist_observation: Is there a documented process for employees to provide feedback on safety procedures, PPE adequacy, and workplace improvements?
questions.auditor_verification:
Document Verification: 
Suggestion/feedback system procedure, registers, digital logs.

Shopfloor Verification: 
Verify feedback boxes, QR systems, suggestion formats at workplaces.
questions.observation: Procedure is available. Suggestion/Feedback boxes are provided at canteen and block entrances.
questions.recommendations: Improve feedback implementation by tracking and closing suggestions within defined timelines. Display status updates as per ISO 45001:2018 Clause 10.3.

questions.checklist_observation: Do employees actively participate in safety inspections, internal audits, and incident investigations?
questions.auditor_verification:
Document Verification: 
Participation rosters for audits & GEMBAs.

Shopfloor Verification: 
Ask employees about their audit involvement.
questions.observation: Employees are not actively participating in inspections and audits.
questions.recommendations: Involve shopfloor employees in Risk Assessment and PHA exercises. Include employee representatives in safety inspections as per ISO 45001:2018 Clause 5.4.

questions.checklist_observation: Are EHS induction and refresher training programs conducted for all categories of employees, including contract workers?
questions.auditor_verification:
Document Verification: 
Induction/training attendance, training matrix.

Shopfloor Verification: 
Ask new employees/contractors about training received.
questions.observation: EHS induction training is provided.
questions.recommendations: Include Process Safety modules during EHS induction training as per OSHA PSM 29 CFR 1910.119.

questions.checklist_observation: Are EHS representatives or safety champions nominated in each department or work area?
questions.auditor_verification:
Document Verification: 
Check nomination letters, champion list, roles assigned.

Shopfloor Verification: 
Verify champion name displayed in each area.
questions.observation: No procedure exists for selecting Safety Champions.
questions.recommendations: Develop a procedure for nominating and selecting Safety Champions in each department as per ISO 45001:2018 Clause 5.4 and OISD-GDN-192.

questions.checklist_observation: Are SOG (Safety Observation Gemba) & SIG (Safety interaction Gemba) conducted at defined intervals?
questions.auditor_verification:
Document Verification: 
Gemba/SIG records, checklist files.

Shopfloor Verification: 
Verify SIG/SOG points on area boards.
questions.observation: Observation sheets are available for SOG/SIG.
questions.recommendations: Ensure 100% compliance with Gemba round schedule. Track observations and close within defined timelines.

questions.checklist_observation: Is EHS performance information (KPIs, incidents, safety initiatives) regularly communicated and displayed to all employees?
questions.auditor_verification:
Document Verification: 
Monthly dashboards, KPI reports.

Shopfloor Verification: 
Verify displays at shopfloor, notice boards.
questions.observation: Granules Care Chronicle news letter, Town hall meetings etc in place

questions.checklist_observation: Are EHS initiatives and compliance integrated into employees’ Key Result Areas (KRAs) or performance appraisals?
questions.auditor_verification:
Document Verification: 
HR appraisal forms showing EHS participation criteria.

Shopfloor Verification: 
Ask sample employees if EHS KPIs affect their evaluation.
questions.observation: EHS integration into employee KRAs is not evident.
questions.recommendations: Integrate EHS initiatives into employee KRAs and performance appraisals as per ISO 45001:2018 Clause 5.1 and OISD-GDN-206.

questions.checklist_observation: Is employee participation in EHS programs periodically reviewed and analyzed to identify improvement opportunities?
questions.auditor_verification:
Document Verification: 
Monthly/Quarterly participation review reports.

Shopfloor Verification: 
Evidence on shopfloor boards showing engagement trends.
questions.observation: Periodic review of employee participation in EHS programs is not evident.
questions.recommendations: Develop a program for periodic review and analysis of employee participation in EHS activities as per ISO 45001:2018 Clause 9.1.

questions.checklist_observation: Do the Unit participate in National Level Awards on safety?
questions.auditor_verification:
Document Verification: 
Award participation forms, submissions.

Shopfloor Verification: 
Display of awards, trophies, recognition boards.
questions.observation: British Safety Council - ISA 2026 & CII EHS excellence awards - site has applied
questions.recommendations: Enhance communication and documentation for award participation. Maintain JSA worker training records as per ISO 45001:2018 Clause 7.5.

questions.checklist_observation: Has the facility been awarded during last two years?
questions.auditor_verification:
Document Verification: 
Award certificates, emails.

Shopfloor Verification: 
Award displays visible in common areas.
questions.observation: British Safety Council - ISA 2026 - Site has achieved a Pass

questions.checklist_observation: Do the facility celebrate safety week/Day or organize safety exhibition?
questions.auditor_verification:
Document Verification: 
Event plan, communication, attendance sheets.

Shopfloor Verification: 
Posters, event photos displayed.
questions.observation: NSD, Electrical week, Fire week, Process Safety week, Machine safety Week- Trainings  - celebrations

questions.checklist_observation:
Are EHS bulletins provided by the EHS department for all employees?
(To serve as a rapid and succinct medium for publicizing EHS incidents/issues and dissemination of lessons learned.)
questions.auditor_verification:
Document Verification: 
Bulletins, circulations, email communication log.

Shopfloor Verification: 
Lesson learned posters displayed in departments.
questions.observation: EHS bulletins are not available.
questions.recommendations: Develop and implement EHS bulletins for disseminating lessons learned and safety alerts as per Factories Act 1948 Section 41B and OISD-GDN-206.

questions.checklist_observation:
Is a monthly EHS awareness sessions organized for the personnel? 
Does the content of the awareness sessions focus on relevant and current EHS issues and requirements?
questions.auditor_verification:
Document Verification: 
Awareness calendar, attendance records.

Shopfloor Verification: 
Check awareness posters & session topic boards.
questions.observation: CRT trainings and TBTs are in place.
questions.recommendations: Improve training effectiveness by conducting assessments and incorporating feedback as per ISO 45001:2018 Clause 7.2.

questions.checklist_observation: Does a management system exist to properly identify, interpret, and maintain the relevant internal and external codes, standards, and other documents that set forth either requirements or guidance followed in the design, operations, and maintenance of processes and equipment included in the EHS program?
questions.auditor_verification:
Document Verification: 
Legal compliance procedure, legal register, statutory matrix, update logs.

Shopfloor Verification: 
Check onsite validity of displayed statutory licenses/permits.
Ensure field conditions match the legal requirements.
questions.observation: No management system exists for identifying and maintaining applicable codes, standards, and regulatory documents as required under PSM Element 1 (OSHA 29 CFR 1910.119).
questions.recommendations: Develop Standards & Codes Management Program as per OSHA PSM 29 CFR 1910.119(d) and IS 14489 covering: applicable regulations, review process, and communication.

questions.checklist_observation: Is a legal register developed based on applicable statutory regulations on occupational health and safety?
questions.auditor_verification:
Document Verification: 
Complete legal register, inclusion of central/state rules.

Shopfloor Verification: 
Sample check statutory compliance in field.
questions.observation: Legal register available via EY Compliance Tool. Personnel lack understanding of requirements under Factories Act 1948, Environment Protection Act 1986, and state-specific rules.
questions.recommendations: Provide training on Factories Act 1948, EPA 1986, and applicable state rules to all accountable personnel.

questions.checklist_observation: is the legal register reviewed and updated periodically to include changes in the regulatory requirements
questions.auditor_verification:
Document Verification: 
Revision history, evidence of periodic review.

Shopfloor Verification: 
Confirm newly amended rules visible in field compliance.
questions.observation: Legal register updated via EY Compliance Tool. No defined review frequency as per ISO 14001:2015 Clause 6.1.3. No training on regulatory updates.
questions.recommendations: Define review frequency as per ISO 14001:2015 Clause 6.1.3. Conduct quarterly training on regulatory changes.

questions.checklist_observation: Are the applicable licences for concerned unit are being identified and are tracked on a regular basis?
questions.auditor_verification:
Document Verification: 
License master list (CFO/CFE, Fire NOC, Factory License, PESO).

Shopfloor Verification: 
Verify license display where required; check validity.
questions.observation: All applicable licenses identified and tracked regularly through EY Compliance Tool as per Factories Act 1948.

questions.checklist_observation: Are with roles and responsibilities defined to ensure compliance to applicable legal requirements?
questions.auditor_verification:
Document Verification: 
Roles & Responsiblities matrix for legal compliance, accountability defined.

Shopfloor Verification: 
Ask area managers about legal responsibilities.
questions.observation: Roles for legal compliance defined via EY Compliance Tool. No training on accountability as required under ISO 45001:2018 Clause 5.3.
questions.recommendations: Provide training on compliance responsibilities as per ISO 45001:2018 Clause 7.2 and 7.3.

questions.checklist_observation: Are the evaluation results of compliance with legal & standard requirements are discussed in management review meetings?
questions.auditor_verification:
Document Verification: 
MOM of management review, compliance evaluation report.

Shopfloor Verification: 
Check implementation of decisions taken during MRM (corrected controls).
questions.observation: Compliance evaluation discussed in Management Review Meetings as per ISO 14001:2015 Clause 9.3. MOM records maintained.

questions.checklist_observation: Is there a full time and qualified EHS personnel is available in the Unit?
questions.auditor_verification:
Document Verification: 
Qualification certificates; appointment letter.

Shopfloor Verification: 
Verify physical presence of EHS officer.
questions.observation: Full-time qualified EHS personnel available as per Factories Act 1948 Section 40-B and State Factory Rules.

questions.checklist_observation: Are integrity tests conducted on buildings / structures and documents maintained?
questions.auditor_verification:
Document Verification: 
Structural stability certificate, roof inspection reports.

Shopfloor Verification: 
Check structural condition—cracks, corrosion, safe access.
questions.observation: Building integrity tests conducted but checklist not fully developed as per IS 456:2000 and National Building Code 2016.
questions.recommendations: Develop Building Inspection Checklist as per IS 456:2000 and NBC 2016 with assessment criteria and frequency.

questions.checklist_observation: Is a proper Hazardous waste authorization obtained from regulatory authorities for disposal of waste and is valid?
questions.auditor_verification:
Document Verification: 
Valid HW authorization, Form‑IV, Form‑5 submissions.

Shopfloor Verification: 
HW storage area compliance, labels, secondary containment.
questions.observation: Valid Hazardous Waste Authorization from TGPCB as per Hazardous Waste Management Rules 2016.

questions.checklist_observation: Is there valid Consent to Operate (CFO/CFE) from the State pollution control board? (Give the latest compliance report submitted to the PCB.)
questions.auditor_verification:
Document Verification: 
CFO/CFE, latest submissions to PCB.

Shopfloor Verification: 
Verify operations match consent capacity (air/effluent).
questions.observation: Valid Consent to Operate from TGPCB as per Water Act 1974 and Air Act 1981. Compliance reports submitted.

questions.checklist_observation: Does the Compliance to Consent quanitities and Recommendations ensured?
questions.auditor_verification:
Document Verification: 
Monthly water/air logs, stack emission compliance reports.

Shopfloor Verification: 
Inspect ETP, scrubber, boiler stack operations for compliance.

questions.checklist_observation:
Does the emergency response training plan for emergency response personnel cover the following areas?
- Pre-emergency planning and coordination with outside parties?
- Personnel roles, lines of authority, training, and communication?
- Emergency recognition and prevention?
- Safe distances and places of refuge?
- Site security?
- Evacuation routes and procedure?
- Decontamination procedures?
- Emergency medical treatment and first aid?
- Emergency alerting and response procedures?
- Critique or response and follow-up?
- Personal Protective Equipment to be worn and procedures for handling emergency incidents?
- Emergency equipment?
- Standard Operating Procedures?
questions.auditor_verification:
Document Verification:Review the Emergency Response Training Plan / Training Module to confirm coverage of:
# Pre-emergency planning & coordination (fire dept., hospitals, mutual aid)
# Defined roles, responsibilities, and communication hierarchy (ERT structure)
# Emergency recognition & prevention aspects
Safe distance criteria and places of refuge / assembly points
# Site security procedures during emergencies
Evacuation routes, maps, and SOPs
# Decontamination procedures (especially for chemical exposure cases)
# Emergency medical response (first aid, BLS, ambulance arrangements)
# Alarm/alerting and communication protocols
# Post-incident actions (critique, reporting, follow-up)
# PPE matrix for different emergency scenarios
# List & operation of emergency equipment
# Applicable SOPs for different emergency situations
Verify the training curriculum / syllabus / presentation content includes all above elements
# Check training attendance records for ERT members and emergency response personnel
# Verify training frequency (initial + refresher) and training plan coverage
# Review training assessment records (pre/post test, competency validation)
Shopfloor:
Ask ERT members:
“What is your role during an emergency?”
“How do you communicate during emergency?”
“What PPE will you use for fire / chemical spill?”
Ask employees:
“Where will you go during evacuation?”
“How will you identify emergency alarm?”
Verify physically:
Emergency equipment (SCBA, fire suits, stretchers, spill kits) availability & familiarity
Display of evacuation routes and assembly points
Availability of PPE relevant to emergency scenarios

Conduct scenario-based questioning:
“What will you do in case of chemical spill?”
“How do you handle injured person during emergency?”

questions.checklist_observation:
Does the organization establish, implement and maintain a procedure(s) for dealing with Process safety Events and for taking corrective action and preventive action. The procedure(s) shall define requirements for: 
a) identifying and correcting nonconformity(is) and taking action(s) to mitigate their environmental impacts
b) investigating nonconformity(is), determining their cause(s) and taking actions in order to avoid their recurrence,
c) evaluating the need for action(s) to prevent nonconformity(is) and implementing appropriate actions designed to avoid their occurrence, 
d) recording the results of corrective action(s) and preventive action(s) taken, and 
e) reviewing the effectiveness of corrective action(s) and preventive action(s) taken.

a) Tier 1 - Primary containment loss with serious consequences
b) Tier 2 - Primary containment loss with lesser consequences
c) Tier 3 - Near misses and challenges to safety systems
d) Tier 4 - Operating discipline and management system indicators
Refer to API RP 754:2016 and OISD-STD-154.

questions.observation:
1) Preventive maintenance for the all safety relief valve (SRV) is being performed annually instead of at the specified quarterly frequency. Delayed inspection may allow deterioration or malfunction to remain undetected. Follow the approved quarterly schedule and document each inspection, test result, defect, and corrective action.

2) Calibration records/certificates for the Safety Relief Valve (SRV) associated with the nitrogen blanketing system in the tank farm area were not available for verification. Absence of valid calibration records may affect the reliability of overpressure protection and compromise the safe operation of storage tanks under nitrogen blanketing conditions.
questions.recommendations:
1) Restore the approved quarterly SRV inspection and test schedule, update the asset register and due-date tracker, and evaluate all overdue valves before continued service. Record set pressure, test results, defects, corrective actions, certification, and independent review.

2) Obtain or perform traceable calibration for the nitrogen-blanketing SRV through a competent agency and verify the set pressure against approved design data. Quarantine overdue or uncertified devices, update the valve register, and track future calibration due dates.

questions.observation: The pressure vessel management system is not fully effective, as statutory inspection, record maintenance, tagging, and compliance monitoring requirements under Factories Act/Form-10 are not adequately ensured across the site.

questions.checklist_observation:
Does the OHC have the following –
• Facilities available to handle emergency cases and provide first aid
• Ambulance permanently stationed at the facility with all amenities
• Bed space available (as per Factories Act)
questions.auditor_verification:
Document:
Emergency facility checklist, ambulance fitness documents.
Shopfloor:
Check availability of beds, first‑aid equipment, working ambulance.
questions.observation:
1) Medicine inventory and stock levels are not being adequately maintained in the occupational health center. Essential medicines may be unavailable or expired when needed. Establish minimum and maximum stock levels, expiry tracking, storage-condition checks, periodic inventory review, and documented replenishment responsibilities.

2) A current list of hazardous chemicals used or stored at the site is not available in the occupational health center. Medical personnel may lack critical information for exposure assessment and treatment. Maintain an updated chemical inventory with SDS access, hazard classification, likely exposure routes, and emergency treatment guidance.

3) Inventory records for medical materials and consumables were not being maintained. Lack of stock management may result in shortages of critical medical supplies during emergencies.

4) List of hazardous chemicals handled at the site was not available in the OHC. Absence of this information may delay appropriate medical treatment during chemical exposure incidents.

5) Oxygen cylinder was last filled in 2024 and no evidence of annual refilling was available. Lack of periodic refilling may affect oxygen availability during medical emergencies.

6) Spare oxygen cylinder trolley was not available in the OHC. Absence of a trolley may delay transportation and deployment of oxygen cylinders during emergencies.

7) Dedicated ambulance driver was not available for emergency transportation. Non-availability of a trained ambulance driver may result in delays in medical evacuation and emergency response.
questions.recommendations:
1) Implement a controlled medical inventory system with item codes, minimum/maximum levels, batch and expiry tracking, storage-condition monitoring, periodic reconciliation, and replenishment responsibilities. Quarantine expired or damaged stock and document disposal.

2) Maintain a controlled, current hazardous-chemical inventory in the OHC linked to approved SDS, exposure routes, symptoms, first-aid measures, antidote requirements, and emergency contacts. Establish change notification from procurement, production, and EHS and review the list periodically.

3) Implement an item-wise inventory register for medicines and consumables with minimum/maximum stock, batch, expiry, storage conditions, issue, and replenishment tracking. Perform periodic reconciliation and quarantine expired or damaged materials.

4) Maintain a controlled hazardous-chemical list in the OHC linked to current SDS, exposure routes, symptoms, first aid, antidotes, and emergency contacts. Require EHS notification for additions or changes and review the list at a defined frequency.

5) Have the oxygen cylinder inspected, pressure and contents verified, and refilled or replaced by an authorized agency before emergency use. Establish cylinder identification, fill and hydro-test tracking, minimum reserve quantity, routine pressure checks, and expiry alerts.

6) Provide a compatible, stable oxygen-cylinder trolley with secure restraints and wheels suitable for emergency movement. Keep it accessible, inspect it routinely, and train OHC staff in safe cylinder handling and transport.

7) Provide continuous emergency transport coverage through a dedicated trained ambulance driver or a documented roster with competent backups. Define response-time expectations, verify licences and fitness, test call-out arrangements, and record drill performance.

questions.observation:
1) Steam line leakages were observed at multiple locations. Leakage from steam lines can result in energy loss, reduced system efficiency, and potential burn hazards to personnel working in the vicinity.

2) Leakage is present at flanges and pump seals in the hot-oil system. Escaping hot oil can cause burns, slips, fire, and equipment damage.

3) Pump seal leakages and pipeline flange leakages were observed in the boiler area. The identified leakages may result in loss of utility media, reduced system efficiency, housekeeping issues, and increased risk of personnel exposure to hot fluids or steam.
questions.recommendations:
1) Identify, isolate, and repair all steam leaks using an approved leak register and priority based on pressure, temperature, and personnel exposure. Replace defective traps, gaskets, valves, or insulation as applicable, barricade hazardous locations, and verify leak-free restoration.

2) Isolate and repair the leaking points, inspect gaskets and seals, clean contaminated surfaces, and implement periodic leak checks and preventive maintenance.

3) Identify, isolate, and repair all pump-seal and flange leaks using compatible seals and gaskets. Barricade hot-fluid exposure areas, clean contamination, verify leak-free restoration under operating conditions, and establish routine leak inspections and failure trending.

2) Establish a periodic inspection and maintenance program, tag each trolley, and remove defective units from service until repaired.

3) Create an asset-wise preventive-maintenance program for hydraulic trolleys covering brakes, wheels, hydraulics, structure, handles, and load stability. Tag each trolley, record inspections and repairs, and remove overdue or defective units from service.

questions.observation:
1) A retrofit has been installed on the DG set without following the formal change-control process. Unassessed changes may introduce electrical, mechanical, fire, emissions, or reliability risks and may invalidate documentation. Initiate retrospective management of change, complete technical and safety reviews, update drawings and procedures, and obtain approval before continued use.

2) A retrofit emission control device has been installed on the DG Set; however, no formal Management of Change (MOC)/Change Control documentation was available for verification. Absence of a documented change control process may result in inadequate assessment of technical, operational, environmental, and safety impacts associated with the modification.
questions.recommendations:
1) Initiate retrospective Management of Change for the DG-set retrofit, including technical, electrical, mechanical, fire, environmental, and reliability assessments. Update drawings, manuals, spares, training, and maintenance requirements, close pre-startup actions, and obtain approval for continued operation.

2) Initiate retrospective Management of Change for the DG-set emission-control retrofit, covering technical, electrical, fire, emissions, structural, and operational impacts. Update drawings and procedures, close risk actions, train affected personnel, and obtain approval before continued operation.

questions.checklist_observation: Whether walkways are clearly marked and free from obstruction?
questions.auditor_verification:

questions.observation:
1) Centrifuge wet material is being stored on the walkways at both the ground floor and first floor of Production Block-1. This obstructs safe access and egress routes, creates housekeeping issues, and increases the risk of slips, trips, falls, and emergency evacuation difficulties.

2) Methocarbomol material from centrifuge is being stored on the walkways at the ground floor of Production Block-5. This obstructs safe access and egress routes, creates housekeeping issues, and increases the risk of slips, trips, falls, and emergency evacuation difficulties.

3) The front side of the HR Office was found blocked with finished materials. Obstruction of access and movement areas may affect safe pedestrian movement, hinder emergency evacuation, and impact overall housekeeping standards.
questions.recommendations:
1) Remove the centrifuge wet material from walkways immediately and store it in a designated, labelled containment area on suitable pallets. Mark and maintain minimum aisle and emergency-egress widths, and include obstruction checks in shift inspections.

2) Remove the material from the walkway and store it in a designated, labelled area with suitable pallets and containment. Maintain marked pedestrian and emergency routes, define storage limits, and verify aisle clearance during every shift.

3) Remove finished materials from the HR Office frontage and restore the designated pedestrian and emergency-access route. Mark a no-storage zone, provide an approved alternate storage location, and include access clearance in daily housekeeping inspections.

questions.checklist_observation: Do workers follow safe procedures for storage of materials?

questions.observation:
1) Damaged pallets are being used for material storage in the warehouse, and material stacking practices are inadequate. Engineering warehouse materials are stored improperly, creating potential safety hazards. Damaged pallets should be replaced, and proper storage and stacking procedures should be implemented to ensure safe and organized material handling.

2) 1st crop material was found stagnated on the ground floor and first floor of Block-I. Accumulation of material in production areas may affect housekeeping standards, obstruct movement, and increase the risk of material mix-up or process inefficiencies.

3) A large quantity of finished goods is stored directly on the floor in FG stores 1, 2, and 3. This may obstruct cleaning and access, and create unstable stacking or manual-handling hazards. Store materials on sound pallets or racks with defined aisles, stacking limits, and location identification.

4) Four batches of first-crop material are stored directly on the floor in block-1. This can cause contamination or damage, obstruct movement and cleaning, and create manual-handling and housekeeping hazards.
questions.recommendations:
1) Remove damaged pallets from service and replace them with load-rated pallets or racks. Define stacking height and load limits, maintain clear aisles, identify storage locations, and implement documented pallet and housekeeping inspections.

2) Transfer first-crop material to identified pallets or racks in a designated status-controlled area. Define maximum holding time, quantity limits, ownership, and disposal or processing actions; keep aisles clear and verify compliance through daily housekeeping inspections.

3) Transfer finished goods from the floor to load-rated pallets or racks in designated locations. Define stacking and rack-load limits, maintain marked aisles and fire-system clearances, inspect pallet condition, and include floor-storage prohibition in warehouse checks.

4) Transfer the material to identified pallets or racks in a designated area and maintain clear aisles and status labelling.

This may lead to ineffective inventory control, delayed spill response, and improper utilization of spill response materials during emergency situations.

2) Spill control kit was not available in the scrap yard area. Absence of spill response equipment may delay the containment and cleanup of oil, fuel, or chemical spills, increasing the risk of environmental contamination, fire hazards, and unsafe working conditions.

3) Spill control kit was not available at the DG Set diesel storage area. Absence of spill response equipment may delay containment and cleanup of diesel spills, increasing the risk of soil contamination, fire hazards, and unsafe working conditions.
questions.recommendations:
1) Assign a unique ID to every spill kit and issue an approved SOP covering contents, location, inspection frequency, replenishment, use, waste disposal, and escalation. Maintain a master register and seal or tag each kit after inspection.

2) Provide a uniquely identified spill kit sized and equipped for credible scrap-yard oil, fuel, and chemical spills. Define inspection and replenishment requirements, train users, display response instructions, and ensure collected waste is managed through the approved disposal route.

3) Provide a uniquely identified diesel-compatible spill kit at the DG-set storage area with absorbents, drain protection, PPE, waste bags, and response instructions. Inspect and replenish it routinely, train users, and link spill waste to the approved disposal process.

questions.observation:
1) Diesel storage drums located near the powerhouse are maintained without adequate secondary containment. In addition, the identification tag affixed to a full diesel drum incorrectly indicates that the drum is empty.

2) Hydrochloric acid (HCl) and isopropyl alcohol (IPA) are stored within the production block-3 without secondary containment. A leak or spill could spread into work areas, causing chemical exposure, environmental contamination, and fire risk in the case of IPA.

3) Warehouse liquid storage drums lack secondary containment. Provide self-contained spill containment pallets to prevent spills, enhance workplace safety, and protect the environment.

4) Dimethyl carbonate is stored or handled without secondary containment. A leak or spill could spread to surrounding areas and generate flammable vapor.

5) Chemical drums in the warehouse are not consistently placed on self-contained spill pallets. Leakage could spread across the floor, expose personnel, and mix with incompatible materials.

6) Biodiesel drums are stored without self-contained spill pallets infront of warehouse. A leak could spread to surrounding areas and create slip, environmental, and fire hazards.
questions.recommendations:
1) Place all diesel drums in a designated, protected storage area with compatible secondary containment sized for the credible spill. Correct the status label immediately and implement container identification, inventory reconciliation, inspection, and segregation controls.

2) Provide compatible, adequately sized spill-containment pallets and segregate incompatible chemicals.

3) Place all liquid drums on compatible, load-rated spill-containment pallets sized for the credible release. Maintain segregation, closure, labels, aisle clearance, and routine documented inspection; remove leaking containers from service immediately.

4) Provide a compatible spill-containment pallet of adequate capacity and ensure containers remain closed, labelled, and protected from ignition sources.

5) Provide compatible containment pallets of adequate capacity for all drums and maintain chemical segregation and inspection controls.

6) Place the drums on compatible secondary containment of adequate capacity and maintain proper labelling, segregation, and inspection.

questions.observation:
1) Near BD/SSR-104-01 in block-1, a plastic drum is covered with a plastic sheet and exposed to a high-temperature environment. Exposure to elevated temperatures may cause deterioration of the drum and cover, potentially leading to material degradation, leakage, pressure build-up, or fire hazards depending on the contents stored.

2) Approximately 3 tonnes of Methocarbon material was found stored at the rear side of the gate under a tarpaulin cover. Storage of material in an undesignated outdoor location may lead to deterioration of material quality, environmental exposure, housekeeping concerns, and potential safety risks.

3) Flammable solvent drums are being stored open and exposed to direct sunlight in the open area near the lift at Block-III. Heat exposure and open containers can increase vapor generation, spillage, and fire risk.

4) Limit storage to the required 2 drums at the point of use and relocate the remaining drums to a designated fuel storage area.

questions.recommendations:

Confirm container material compatibility and temperature limits from the approved SDS, replace degraded packaging, and prohibit temporary plastic-sheet covers.

2) Move the approximately 3 tonnes of material to an approved covered warehouse or engineered temporary storage area with pallets, weather protection, drainage control, identification, and inventory status. Assess material quality before use and prohibit storage near gates or emergency access routes.

3) Keep the drums closed and relocate them to a shaded, ventilated, designated flammable-liquid storage area with secondary containment.

4) Ensure proper stacking, secondary containment, and maintain clear, unobstructed walkways in accordance with industrial safety requirements.

5) Relocate it to a designated fuel storage area with secondary containment, identification, segregation, and firefighting provisions.

questions.observation:

2) Overflow protection is not available for solvent transfer from the tank farm to the production blocks. A receiving vessel could be overfilled, causing spills, vapor release, and fire. Install independent high-level alarms and automatic transfer shutdown interlocks, and verify their operation through periodic proof testing.
questions.recommendations:

questions.checklist_observation: Does Plant has identified & eliminated all Open handling activities of solvents for cleaning equipment, equipment parts and accessories in process areas and WH
questions.auditor_verification:
Document: Solvent handling SOP, closed cleaning/transfer procedure, risk assessment, improvement records.
Shopfloor: Verify no open solvent handling, closed transfer systems, proper containers, ventilation, and ignition source control.
questions.observation:
1) Recovered toluene generated after distillation is being transferred in drums from block-3. Open or manual drum transfer can lead to spills, vapor exposure, static discharge, and fire.

2) Sodium methoxide is being mixed with methanol in an open stainless-steel container during solution preparation in block-5. Open handling may release flammable methanol vapors and expose personnel to a highly reactive chemical, creating fire and contact hazards.

3) Methanol is being used for utensil cleaning without a documented justification or approved risk assessment. Its high flammability and toxicity may expose personnel to unnecessary vapor, fire, and skin-contact hazards.

4) PCF unloading is being performed in an open condition in block-1. This may expose personnel to dust, vapors, splashes, and uncontrolled material release. Provide a closed unloading arrangement with suitable extraction or containment, earthing where required, appropriate PPE, and a documented procedure.
questions.recommendations:
1) Replace open drum transfer with a closed, bonded and earthed transfer system using compatible piping, pumps, hoses, dry-break couplings, vapor control, and secondary containment. Define transfer limits, pre-transfer checks, spill response, and inspection requirements.

2) Replace open mixing with a closed, inerted and bonded system designed for sodium methoxide and methanol compatibility. Provide controlled addition, ventilation, temperature monitoring, spill containment, emergency isolation, and an approved operating procedure based on reaction-risk assessment.

3) Evaluate safer substitutes and, if methanol remains necessary, define closed handling, ventilation, PPE, storage, and waste controls in an approved procedure.

4) Provide a closed PCF unloading system with compatible connections, local extraction or containment, bonding/earthing where required, and spill control. Validate performance, define pre-use checks and PPE, train operators, and document the unloading procedure.

questions.observation:
1) The earth plate at the GFN spent mixed solvent unloading area was found in a rusted condition near the steps. Corrosion of earthing components may affect the effectiveness of the grounding system and increase the risk of static charge accumulation during solvent unloading operations.

2) The Earth-Rite static grounding system in the tank farm is not functioning. Solvent transfer without verified grounding can allow static charge to accumulate and ignite flammable vapors. Repair and test the system immediately, prevent transfer until grounding is confirmed, and include functional checks in the unloading checklist.
questions.recommendations:
1) Clean or replace the corroded earth plate, protect it with an approved corrosion-control method that does not insulate contact surfaces, and verify continuity and earth resistance. Label the point, record results, and include it in scheduled inspection and testing.

2) Stop solvent transfer until the Earth-Rite system is repaired and a valid ground is proven. Function-test the interlock and clamp, calibrate where applicable, include a pass/fail check in every unloading checklist, and retain preventive-maintenance records.

questions.observation:

2) Assess the UPS battery technology and fire hazards and install compatible early detection and automatic suppression or other engineered protection. Provide ventilation and gas monitoring where required, integrate alarms, control ignition sources, and proof-test the system periodically.

3) Provide a suitable, approved extinguisher for energized electrical equipment at an accessible, clearly marked location outside the immediate hazard zone. Add it to the fire-equipment register and implement monthly inspection and scheduled competent-person servicing.

questions.observation:
1) Security personnel have not received adequate training on emergency response procedures, including alarm activation, emergency communication, evacuation coordination, and incident escalation.

2) Security personnel have not received adequate training on their roles and responsibilities during emergency situations. This may delay alarm activation, communication, access control, evacuation support, and incident escalation.
questions.recommendations:
1) Deliver documented, scenario-based emergency-response training to all security personnel covering alarm activation, emergency calls, access control, evacuation support, muster coordination, and escalation. Assess competency through drills and retrain personnel who do not meet the acceptance criteria.

2) Provide documented scenario-based training, define individual duties, conduct drills, and periodically assess competency.

questions.observation: Senario based risk assessment is not done
questions.recommendations: Conduct scenario-based emergency risk assessments for credible fire, explosion, toxic release, spill and utility-failure events. Define resources and response actions and validate assumptions through scheduled drills.

questions.checklist_observation: Does the OSEP describe PPE and emergency equipment?
questions.auditor_verification:
Document: On-Site Emergency Plan, PPE matrix, emergency equipment list, inspection/checklist records.
Shopfloor: Verify availability, accessibility, condition, and location of emergency PPE and equipment as per OSEP.
questions.observation:
1) An ammonia leakage emergency kit is not available in ammonia purging area in block-3. Personnel may be unable to safely control or respond to an ammonia release. Provide a complete, clearly located kit including suitable respiratory and chemical protective equipment, leak-control tools, instructions, and periodic inspection.

2) Ammonia gas cylinder area in the fabrication shed was not provided with an ammonia leakage control/emergency leak response kit. Absence of a suitable leakage kit may delay emergency response during ammonia leaks, increasing the risk of personnel exposure and escalation of the incident.

3) Snake catcher equipment was not available in the Security Office Room. Absence of suitable snake handling equipment may delay safe response to snake sightings within the premises, increasing the risk of injury to personnel and unsafe handling practices.
questions.recommendations:
1) Provide a complete ammonia emergency kit at an accessible upwind location, including chemical-resistant PPE, suitable respiratory protection, leak-control tools, detection, instructions, and emergency contacts. Inspect contents and expiry routinely and train responders through drills.

2) Provide a complete ammonia leak-control and emergency-response kit at an accessible upwind location, including suitable respiratory and chemical PPE, leak-control tools, detection, and instructions. Inspect routinely and train designated responders through drills.

3) Provide approved snake-handling equipment in the Security Office and restrict use to trained designated responders. Establish a safe response procedure, emergency contact with an authorized wildlife or rescue service, equipment inspection, and incident reporting requirements.

questions.checklist_observation:
Does the emergency response training plan for emergency response personnel cover the following areas?
- Pre-emergency planning and coordination with outside parties?
- Personnel roles, lines of authority, training, and communication?
- Emergency recognition and prevention?
- Safe distances and places of refuge?
- Site security?
- Evacuation routes and procedure?
- Decontamination procedures?
- Emergency medical treatment and first aid?
- Emergency alerting and response procedures?
- Critique or response and follow-up?
- Personal Protective Equipment to be worn and procedures for handling emergency incidents?
- Emergency equipment?
- Standard Operating Procedures?
questions.auditor_verification:
Document Verification:Review the Emergency Response Training Plan / Training Module to confirm coverage of:
# Pre-emergency planning & coordination (fire dept., hospitals, mutual aid)
# Defined roles, responsibilities, and communication hierarchy (ERT structure)
# Emergency recognition & prevention aspects
Safe distance criteria and places of refuge / assembly points
# Site security procedures during emergencies
Evacuation routes, maps, and SOPs
# Decontamination procedures (especially for chemical exposure cases)
# Emergency medical response (first aid, BLS, ambulance arrangements)
# Alarm/alerting and communication protocols
# Post-incident actions (critique, reporting, follow-up)
# PPE matrix for different emergency scenarios
# List & operation of emergency equipment
# Applicable SOPs for different emergency situations
Verify the training curriculum / syllabus / presentation content includes all above elements
# Check training attendance records for ERT members and emergency response personnel
# Verify training frequency (initial + refresher) and training plan coverage
# Review training assessment records (pre/post test, competency validation)
Shopfloor:
Ask ERT members:
“What is your role during an emergency?”
“How do you communicate during emergency?”
“What PPE will you use for fire / chemical spill?”
Ask employees:
“Where will you go during evacuation?”
“How will you identify emergency alarm?”
Verify physically:
Emergency equipment (SCBA, fire suits, stretchers, spill kits) availability & familiarity
Display of evacuation routes and assembly points
Availability of PPE relevant to emergency scenarios

Conduct scenario-based questioning:
“What will you do in case of chemical spill?”
“How do you handle injured person during emergency?”

Does the organization establish, implement and maintain a procedure(s) for dealing with Process safety Events and for taking corrective action and preventive action. The procedure(s) shall define requirements for:

b) investigating nonconformity(is), determining their cause(s) and taking actions in order to avoid their recurrence,

questions.observation:

Ambulance related issues

• Expired medicines (Pantodex injection expired in June'2026) was observed in Ambulance First aid box

questions.recommendations:
1. Prepare and display hazardous chemicals list at OHC with first aid procedures as required by Factories Act 1948 Rule 68-J and MSDS requirements.
Ambulance related issues
• Provide clear and durable ID and safety labels at the point of use, and add label condition and legibility to routine inspections.
• Immediately remove and safely dispose of expired medical items, refill approved stock, and put in place a written monthly expiry check with responsible person’s sign-off.

• Renew the ambulance insurance, fitness certificate and road tax before further use, and keep a compliance tracker with renewal reminders.

• Create a defect-reporting and escalation log for ambulance issues, including owner, target date, closure evidence and check before each shift.
• Remove or replace the overdue extinguisher immediately, complete servicing by an authorized agency, and add due-date reminders to the inspection register.
• Assign the ambulance driver responsibility for the pre-use vehicle condition check, train the driver on the checklist, and require signed check before each shift.

Define method-selection criteria based on process complexity, hazard severity, employee exposure, process age and operating history. OSHA 29 CFR 1910.119(e)(1)-(2).

Therefore, the selected study method may not match the complexity and hazard potential of each process.
questions.recommendations: Add a methodology-selection matrix: use detailed HAZOP for complex/high-hazard processes, What-If/Checklist for simpler changes, and FMEA or Fault Tree Analysis where equipment failure or event logic requires it. questions.checklist_observation: Are all the following factors considered in the visual inspection program: the condition of the outside of equipment, insulation, painting/coatings, supports and attachments, and identifying mechanical damage, corrosion, vibration, leakage or improper components or repairs?
questions.auditor_verification:
Document: Visual inspection checklist, schedule, inspection reports, defect records.
Shopfloor: Verify equipment condition, insulation, coating, supports, corrosion, vibration, leakage, and repairs.
questions.observation:
1. Utility lines, Brine tanks, PB-I Technical area 1st Floor most of the lines and equipments were observed to be corroded 
2. Visual inspection is available for Pressure vessels & Reactors. For auxiliary equipment it is missing like Pipelines, Brine tanks.
3. Cable tray supports rusted and damaged at QC washroom area.
4. I/ST/007 - 5 KL receiver nozzle connected to level indicator is fully corroded at PB-I Day Tank Storage Tank area
5.Insulation is required for the MDC receiver.
6. Street light insulation sleeve damaged and module box corroded in front of QC
questions.recommendations:
1. Carry out a comprehensive corrosion survey of utility lines, brine tanks, pipelines and equipment in the PB-I technical area; repair or replace degraded components, apply a suitable protective coating, and set up regular corrosion monitoring.
2. Extend the written visual-inspection program to all auxiliary equipment, including pipelines, brine tanks, supports, attachments, insulation and coatings, with defined frequency, acceptance criteria and defect-closure tracking.
3. Replace or structurally repair the corroded cable trays and supports at the QC washroom, apply corrosion protection, and inspect the complete cable route for similar deterioration.
4. Remove I/ST/007 from service as required, assess the receiver nozzle and level-indicator connection for remaining thickness and integrity, replace the corroded section, perform a leak test, and return it to service only after competent-person approval.
5. Install chemically and thermally compatible insulation with protective cladding on the MDC receiver and include insulation condition in routine inspections.
6. Replace the damaged street-light insulation sleeve and corroded module box with suitably rated weatherproof components, check electrical insulation and earthing, and put in place regular inspection.

questions.checklist_observation: Is PHA conducted based on the type of change proposed?

questions.recommendations: Create a risk-based PHA selection matrix that specifies when JSA, What-If, HAZOP or another formal study is required. Record the selected method and justification, participants, recommendations, owners and due dates, and prohibit startup until all pre-startup actions are independently verified closed.

questions.checklist_observation:

questions.recommendations: Add a workforce-impact and communication section to the MOC form covering affected roles, competency changes, training needs, operating-regime changes and organizational impacts. Keep a controlled MOC register and require completed training/communication records before startup or use.

questions.checklist_observation: Is the process safety information (hazards of chemicals, process hazards, process technology and process equipment) updated if changed?

questions.observation: PSI procedure is missing just complied using forms, PSI references to be attached to the individual MOC before closure.
questions.recommendations: Prepare and approve a PSI procedure defining document owners, review and update requirements for chemical hazards, process technology, equipment data, P&IDs, design limits and safety systems. For every MOC, identify the affected PSI documents, revise them before startup, check that the documents match the field installation, attach the approved revisions to the MOC and do not close the MOC until the responsible functions confirm completion. OSHA 29 CFR 1910.119(d), 1910.119(i)(2) and 1910.119(l)(4).

questions.checklist_observation: Are the operating procedures or practices updated if changed?

questions.recommendations: Require every MOC to identify affected SOPs and safe-work practices, assign a document owner, complete revision/approval through document control, withdraw superseded versions and train affected workers before startup. Record document numbers, revisions and training evidence in the MOC close-out.

questions.checklist_observation: Who validates the Change (for its applicability) and against which criteria (for its applicability/ non-applicability) to move it to the evaluation phase?

questions.recommendations: Add an MOC applicability screening checklist covering replacement-in-kind, changes to chemicals, process conditions, equipment, facilities, software, procedures and organization. Assign the MOC Coordinator with relevant subject-matter experts to validate the screening, record the reason for applicability or non-applicability, and obtain approval before use. Retain screened-out decisions in the MOC register. OSHA 29 CFR 1910.119(l)(1)-(2).

questions.checklist_observation: Is there review system for effecting any change in the existing plant, equipment or process? Give details of changes or new equipment review (P&I diagram, HAZOP studies, Risk assessment and other documents)
questions.auditor_verification:

questions.checklist_observation: Does the facility have a PSSR procedure that covers new installations, temporary shutdowns, maintenance turnarounds, and extended shutdowns, with or without modifications?

questions.recommendations: Revise site procedure to include a simple PSSR trigger table covering: new facilities; significant modifications; major turnarounds; and restart after temporary or extended shutdown where equipment condition, safeguards, procedures or operating readiness may have changed. questions.recommendations: Add a minor-release procedure with practical limits for quantity, toxicity, flammability, area affected and responder capability. Define when an operator may control the release, mandatory PPE and isolation steps, and clear escalation triggers for alarm activation, ERT response and evacuation.

Before use or startup, assess whether the change affects emergency scenarios, shutdown actions, evacuation routes, assembly points, PPE, response equipment, medical arrangements or external support. Update the onsite emergency plan and train affected workers before closing the MOC. OSHA 29 CFR 1910.119(l)(2)-(5).

For every new or revalidated PHA, compare each emergency scenario with the current onsite emergency plan, record identified gaps and update the plan, resources and training. Close all required emergency-plan actions before startup or PHA closure. OSHA 29 CFR 1910.119(e)(5) and 1910.119(i)(2)(iii).

questions.checklist_observation: Does the OSEP specify that qualified basic life support personnel, as a minimum, also available with medical equipment and transportation capability?
questions.auditor_verification:
Document: Medical preparedness records.  
Shopfloor: Verify ambulance, trained personnel.
questions.observation:
Ambulance related issues 
-First Aid box in ambulance has no ID & contents label
-Expired medicines (Pantodex injection expired in June'2026) was observed in Ambulance First aid box 
-Ambulance driver, was not available in the vehicle - he came after 30 Min. 
-Ambulance - Insurance got expired in May'2026, Fitness & Road tax certificate (expired in 2019) not available 
-Ambulance driver - First aid training certificate not available 
-Training & Expereince records of ambulance driver not available 
-Ambulance siren needs to be relocated, right know it is near to tyres. 
-Ambulance door and latches damaged and pending repair for more than one month.
-No communication record available for reported ambulance issues, fuel, and speedometer concerns.
-The due date of fire extinguisher servicing in the ambulance has expired.
-Ambulance vehicle condition check was not carried out by the driver; it was done by the paramedic."
questions.recommendations:
-Provide durable, clearly visible identification and safety labels at the point of use, and add label condition and legibility to routine inspections.
-Immediately remove and safely dispose of expired medical items, replenish approved stock, and implement a documented monthly expiry check with accountable sign-off.
-Provide a dedicated trained ambulance driver for every shift, maintain a duty roster and backup arrangement, and verify response readiness through periodic drills.
-Renew the ambulance insurance, fitness certificate and road tax before further use, and maintain a compliance tracker with advance renewal alerts.
-Ensure the ambulance driver completes approved first-aid training and retain a valid certificate with refresher due-date tracking.
-Verify the driver's competency and experience, compile the required records, and maintain them in the ambulance personnel file with periodic review.
-Relocate the siren to a protected position that provides effective audible coverage and is not exposed to wheel or road damage; function-test it after installation.
-Repair the ambulance door and latches immediately, prohibit service if secure closure is affected, and close the maintenance request with a functional check.
-Create a defect-reporting and escalation log for ambulance issues, including owner, target date, closure evidence and verification before each shift.
-Remove or replace the overdue extinguisher immediately, complete servicing by an authorized agency, and add advance due-date alerts to the inspection register.
-Assign the ambulance driver responsibility for the pre-use vehicle condition check, train the driver on the checklist, and require signed verification before each shift.

questions.recommendations: Add a methodology-selection matrix: use detailed HAZOP for complex/high-hazard processes, What-If/Checklist for simpler changes, and FMEA or Fault Tree Analysis where equipment failure or event logic requires it.
